name: OneHealthRiskRule
title: StreamFHIR explainable rules
description: The printed rules (hazard and ecological condition) used by the StreamFHIR rule engine. Example canonical URL; these are NOT official HL7, LOINC or SNOMED CT codes.

concept.definition: [condition] When mean of the visual habitat scores <= 5 (of 10). Degraded banks, channel and riparian strip reduce the stream's ability to clean itself and to host life. Advice: Share with the city's river restoration team; repeat the visual check each season.

[condition] When nitrate >= 25 mg/L as NO3 (a conservative screening value, half the French good/moderate boundary of 50) or orthophosphate >= 0.5 mg/L as PO4 (the French good/moderate boundary); one sample is a screening signal, not a status class. Extra nutrients can feed algae; in most fresh waters phosphate is the limiting nutrient, so high phosphate matters most for blooms, while high nitrate mainly signals run-off. Advice: Look upstream for run-off sources (fields, allotments, outfalls) and keep monitoring.

[hazard] When surface = algal-scum, or water-colour = green with water >= 20 C; not counted if the jar/stick test points to ordinary green or filamentous algae. Scums in warm water are typical of cyanobacterial blooms, which can poison dogs, livestock and people. Only a lab test can confirm toxins. If the jar/stick test was not done, the scum is treated as a possible bloom (precaution). Advice: Keep dogs and children out of the water and report the bloom to the local authority for testing.

[hazard] When odour = sewage or water-colour = milky-grey. Sewage smell or grey water suggests faecal contamination, a route for gut infections in people and animals. Advice: Avoid touching the water, wash hands, and report it to the water utility or municipality.

[hazard] When dead-fish = yes. Fish kills point to low oxygen, toxins or pollution - an early warning for other animals. Advice: Do not touch the fish; note how many and report to the environment authority.

concept.display: People in contact with affected water
concept.definition: [hazard] When people-contact = yes while R3 or R4 fired at the site. Exposure turns a water problem into a human-health problem. Advice: Discourage paddling and swimming here until the signal has been checked.

concept.display: Pets or livestock in contact with affected water
concept.definition: [hazard] When animal-contact = yes while R3, R4 or R5 fired at the site. Dogs and livestock drink and swim in affected water and are often the first victims of blooms. Advice: Keep pets and livestock out of the water and away from scum on the shore.

[hazard] When surface = oily-sheen or odour = chemical. Hydrocarbons and chemicals harm aquatic life and can irritate skin on contact. Advice: Avoid skin contact and report the sheen or smell to the environment authority.

concept.display: Nitrate above 50 mg/L (EU Nitrates Directive level)
concept.definition: [condition] When nitrate >= 50 mg/L as NO3: the level at which the EU Nitrates Directive (91/676/EEC, Annex I) treats surface fresh water as affected by pollution; it is also the EU drinking-water parametric value. Stream water is not drinking water, but this level signals run-off that may reach wells and supplies. Advice: Mention it to the water utility; private well owners nearby may want a lab test.

concept.display: No mayfly, stonefly or caddisfly larvae found
concept.definition: [condition] When sensitive-invertebrates = 0 after >= 1 minute of kick-net sampling in a flowing reach. Most families of these groups need clean, oxygen-rich water, so finding none suggests poorer conditions over weeks. Some families tolerate pollution, so this is a coarse screen, not a biotic index. Advice: Repeat the sample in a riffle; if still none, share with the ecology team for a full index.
